Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

certainly adverb

also surely, definitely, undoubtedly, no doubt, without doubt, for certain

classical

Cic. Sen. 11: certē, inquit rīdēns
Verg. A. 1.328: ō dea certē
Traupman 288
Traupman 26: Certē illud legam., sure, I’ll read it
Traupman 211

certē

adverb

certainly, surely; at least

Lewis & Short: of every period and style. Also in answers, and after a concession “at least”: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā (Phaedr. 4 epil. 7).

Other words

  • profectō — certainly, indeed, really

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. 21.30.7: nūllās profectō terrās caelum contingere; Gell. 9.8.1: vērum est profectō; Traupman 288

  • sine dubiō — without doubt, no doubt

    adverbial phrase · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 53.1: erat sine dubiō caelum grave sordidīs nūbibus

    See doubt.

  • nīmīrum — doubtless, of course; often ironic

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 268: nīmīrum hominēs frīgent; Liv. 22.51.4: nōn omnia nīmīrum eīdem dī dedēre

    Lewis & Short: literally “no wonder”; often ironic, “doubtless, to be sure”.

  • certō — for certain (above all in certō sciō, I know for sure)

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.12.3: quod tē molestē ferre certō sciō

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    Lewis & Short: only in the comic poets and in Cicero, most often in his letters; see sure.

  • enimvērō — yes indeed, to be sure; truly (in a reply or a protest)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 1.1.188: Ain' vērō? — Ajō enimvērō. (Lewis & Short s.v. enim); Cic. Verr. 2.1.26: enimvērō ferendum hoc quidem nōn est (Lewis & Short)

    Confirms a reply (“yes, truly”) or puts heat into a protest (“this really is not to be borne”). Traupman 111 gives it for “well, well!”, a surprise it does not express (see well, well!).

Examples

  • ‘certē,’ inquit rīdēns, ‘nam nisi tū āmīsissēs, numquam recēpissem’

    “Certainly,” he said with a laugh, “for if you had not lost it, I would never have taken it back.”Cic. Sen. 11

  • ō dea certē

    a goddess, surely!Verg. A. 1.328

  • nūllās profectō terrās caelum contingere

    that no land, surely, touches the skyLiv. 21.30.7

See also sure, of course, doubt, truly, actually, well, well!.
